title: Baikal Logistics carrier fuel surcharge: 'index reset' versus a mis-keyed contract tier
scenario_text:
Baikal Logistics runs freight-audit-and-pay for a large shipper. This week the accrued freight spend on one contracted carrier, Ternwood Transport, jumped 19% with no volume change. In the #freight-audit Slack channel the audit analyst writes: 'This is the monthly fuel surcharge index reset - DOE diesel ticked up and the surcharge table recalculates on the first business day. Same thing every month, spend always bumps then. Nothing to chase, clearing the exceptions.' The note is timestamped Monday 08:14.

Other systems complicate that. In the TMS (MercuryGate), the rated linehaul base charge - not the fuel line - is what rose; the fuel surcharge line is flat month over month. In the contract-management system, Ternwood's negotiated rate amendment took effect the 1st and moved them from Tier 2 to Tier 3 pricing (a discount deepening from 12% to 18%), meaning rated linehaul should have fallen, not risen. In the freight-pay ledger, 71 invoices since the 1st all rated at the old Tier 1 published tariff. A carrier EDI 210 sample shows Ternwood is billing list rate. And a ServiceNow ticket from a rating clerk opened Sunday night reads: 'The rate engine didn't pick up the new Ternwood contract - I think it fell back to default tariff after the amendment upload failed.'

Each item is dismissible: fuel resets are routine, one clerk ticket is anecdotal, a single tier change is minor. But together - flat fuel, a base-charge rise exactly when a discount should have deepened, 71 invoices at default tariff, EDI showing list rate, and a failed contract upload - they describe the rate engine ignoring a newly negotiated discount and overpaying every invoice, not a benign index reset. The analyst's read predates the clerk's ticket. You own freight audit and the pay run releases tonight. What should you do?
question: What action should the freight-audit owner take before tonight's pay run?

contributor.name: Renata Alvo
contributor.title: Director of Freight Audit and Payment

choices: Accept the fuel-index-reset explanation and release the exceptions; monthly surcharge recalculation routinely bumps carrier spend.

Hold the affected Ternwood invoices and reprocess them against the new Tier 3 amendment now: flat fuel, a base-charge rise where a deeper discount was due, 71 invoices at default tariff, and a failed contract upload show the rate engine is overpaying list rate, not a fuel reset.
Approve the pay run but open a low-priority ticket to reconcile Ternwood's fuel table next month, since each invoice variance is individually small.
Escalate to the carrier's account team to dispute the fuel surcharge index and request a credit for the surcharge overcharge.
